arg_convention: (slot) = (rdi); slot T is the 32-byte entry: [T] head, [T+8] second word, [T+0x10]/[T+0x18] cached key
corrections_to_earlier_packets: #224 confirmed: call site 0x63b0912 passes (slot); the refresh copies the returned node's key, and the returned node is the slot head after restructuring, so the cached key is the new head's key.
#224 refined: the refresh is NOT read-only — 0x63abd00 rewrites +0x28/+0x30/+0x38 links across the whole chain, zeroes [slot+8], and can change [slot].
#219 confirmed: node words +0x28/+0x30/+0x38 and the (+0x20, +0x8) signum idiom are the same ones the slot-insert helper uses; here their roles resolve to parent / next-sibling / first-child.
#217/#219 note: the slot second word [slot+8] is zeroed unconditionally on entry here; its semantic identity is still unresolved, but after this call it is always 0.
return_contract: returns the slot's head node after restructuring; NULL iff the slot is empty; equals [slot] on return in every non-empty case; NOT the global maximum key (tail compares only the last second-round winner against head)
rounds: round 1 over adjacent pairs from node2 onward, larger key wins (ties to later node), loser attached as winner's first child; round 2 only when round 1 yielded >= 2 winners, same pairing over the winner chain; no third round
slot_entry: [slot+8] = 0 on entry, never rewritten, so always 0 on return
unresolved: Semantic identity of [slot+8] (why zeroed here, what it counts between calls).
Why restructuring stops after exactly two pairing rounds instead of running to a single winner.
Purposes of the five non-release callers (FDE 0x63b0980..0x63b15e9 x4, FDE 0x63bc730..0x63bcb12 x1).
Whether later traversals consume the produced tree shape (following +0x38 children) or only the rebuilt +0x30 chain.
What invariant the slot's cached key maintains beyond 'the head's key'.
